polls.description: Growing wave of AI-powered malware, deepfake abuse apps, and nation-state cyberattacks targeting critical infrastructure and users.
polls.question: Should governments prioritize offense or defense against AI-powered cyberattacks?

cluster_stories.title: Hundreds of Mundane AI Apps Are Hiding Sexually Abusive Deepfake Features
cluster_stories.summary: WIRED uncovered some 400 apps and websites linked to Chinese-language developers that look like regular AI tools but had secret features that let users create violent AI-generated images and video.
cluster_stories.headline: 400 AI APPS HIDING DEEPFAKE ABUSE FEATURES... Linked to China

cluster_stories.title: AI-powered malware ‘highly likely’ to be used to hack UK infrastructure by 2028
cluster_stories.summary: National Cyber Security Centre expects attacks on critical facilities such as power stations, airports and hospitalsAI-powered malicious software is “highly likely” to be used in hacking attacks against the UK’s power stations, airports and hospitals by 2028, according to the state cybersecurity body.The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) said AI will probably enable a ransomware attack against critical national infrastructure [CNI] between now and 2028. The UK’s definition of CNI covers a range of facilities and services across sectors including energy, transport, defence, food, health and finance. Continue reading...
cluster_stories.headline: UK CYBER CHIEF: AI MALWARE ATTACKS 'HIGHLY LIKELY' BY 2028

cluster_stories.title: North Korean hackers used AI in crypto heists record $6bn Binance theft
cluster_stories.summary: North Korean hackers may be using AI to plan and carry out cryptocurrency thefts, according to security experts cited in a Bloomberg report published on Monday. They point to the growing complexity and precision of recent attacks, including last week’s record theft from Binance. The use of AI has not been confirmed, and Bloomberg presents […] This story continues at The Next Web
cluster_stories.headline: NORTH KOREA USING AI FOR $6BN BINANCE CRYPTO HEIST

cluster_stories.title: ‘A serious failure’: CPS prosecutor cites imaginary case to high court after AI search
cluster_stories.summary: Exclusive: Nonexistent precedent cited in alleged child rape case adds to dozens of AI-related errors plaguing court proceedingsA senior crown prosecutor acting in a high court case cited an imaginary legal precedent in an error that has sparked fresh concerns about AI hallucinations infecting the justice system.Ravinder Dhillon, representing the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), referenced an entirely made-up case during a dispute over whether a child should be prosecuted for the rape of his younger sister, court documents have revealed. cluster_stories.headline: UK PROSECUTOR CITES FAKE AI CASE IN RAPE TRIAL

cluster_stories.title: Spooky New Infostealer Malware Uses AI to ‘Autodox’ Victims
cluster_stories.summary: Named “Volta-Autodoxer,” the recently uncovered malware uses AI tools to collect troves of data about victims, from login credentials and credit card numbers to Discord sessions and UberEats receipts.
cluster_stories.headline: NEW AI-POWERED MALWARE 'AUTODOXES' VICTIMS

cluster_stories.title: Anthropic denies breach as tampered Claude Code extension hits Cursor users
cluster_stories.summary: A tampered copy of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension sat in Cursor’s extension marketplace for about 11 hours on Thursday 29 October. It reached up to 5,000 users. The malicious versions tried to plant an SSH backdoor on developers’ machines, Cursor said in a security notice. Anthropic says nobody breached its own systems. A security firm […] This story continues at The Next Web
cluster_stories.headline: MALICIOUS CLAUDE EXTENSION HITS 5,000 CURSOR USERS

cluster_stories.title: Google Discloses PageBreak AI Security Agent That Found 500+ XSS Bugs
cluster_stories.summary: According to a paper published by Google, its AI-powered security agent has uncovered more than 500 XSS vulnerabilities across its web applications since entering full operation in January. PageBreak uses Gemini models to autonomously investigate potential vulnerabilities, but reports them only after deterministic validators successfully reproduce the exploit against a running application. By Renato Losio
cluster_stories.headline: GOOGLE'S AI AGENT FINDS 500+ SECURITY BUGS
